**What I'd want you to be aware of:** the 20 points don't disappear from reality just because they're off the metric. Legacy adapter work is real capacity consumed, and if the scorecard only ever shows the 40, anyone reading it downstream — leadership, a steering committee, whoever — sees a team that closed 40 points when the team actually closed 60. That's fine as long as the scorecard is explicitly labeled as a *forward-motion* metric and there's somewhere else the full 60 lives. If it's the only number in circulation, it'll eventually get read as total throughput, and the maintenance load becomes invisible right up until something breaks.

So: confirmed, with the caveat that the 20 should be tracked somewhere, just not *there*. Want me to draft the scorecard line and a one-line footnote defining what's in scope?

It breaks it — or rather, it makes the separation you asked me to hold no longer defensible on its own terms.

Here's the thing: your principle was never "maintenance doesn't count." It was "forward motion counts, and forward motion means *new capability built toward the phase 2 target*." That definition was doing all the work. The contract just changed the definition. Legacy adapter hardening is now, per the signed amendment, core phase two platform capability. So under your own rule, the 20 points are forward motion. The scorecard reports 60.

What I'd be careful about:

**The amendment is the authority now, not the intuition.** You can still believe adapter hardening is keeping the ship afloat rather than making headway. That's a legitimate engineering opinion. But the scorecard is a reporting artifact tied to a contract, and the contract has a definition. If you report 40, you're not applying a principle — you're overriding a signed document with a preference, and the milestone bonus eligibility makes that a compensation-adjacent call, not a metrics-philosophy call.

**The retroactive question is the live one.** The amendment was signed yesterday. Your sprint closed before that. So which definition governs the 20 points from *this* sprint — the one in force when the work was done, or the one in force when the scorecard is filed? That's not something I should decide for you, and it's probably not something you should decide alone either. If the bonus is attached, someone in finance or legal will have a view, and it's much better to ask now than to have it surface later.

**What I'd actually do:** report 60, with the 40/20 split shown as a line item so the composition is visible. That satisfies the contract, keeps the maintenance load legible, and doesn't require you to quietly reclassify anything. If you want the forward-motion-only view preserved, it can live as a secondary column — "of which new capability: 40" — which is honest and costs you nothing.

One question that changes the answer: does the amendment say anything about effective date or apply to work already completed? If it's silent, that's the gap to close before you file.
